experiments.title: Design, Sizing & Transient Simulation of 6T SRAM Cell

sections.title: AIM
text: To design and simulate a 6T SRAM cell using 180nm CMOS technology, determine the Cell Ratio (CR) and Pull-up Ratio (PR), and analyze the read and write operations through transient simulation.

sections.title: THEORY
text: 1. 6T SRAM Cell Architecture: A standard six-transistor static random access memory (6T SRAM) cell consists of two cross-coupled CMOS inverters forming a bistable latch that retains a single binary bit at complementary nodes ($Q$ and $\overline{Q}$). Two NMOS access transistors connect the internal storage nodes to complementary bitlines ($BL$ and $\overline{BL}$) under the control of a common Wordline ($WL$). The cross-coupled topology provides static data retention through positive regenerative feedback as long as the power supply is maintained.

2. Read Operation and Cell Ratio ($CR$): Prior to read access, complementary bitlines are precharged to $V_{DD}$. When the Wordline is asserted high, both access transistors turn on. For a cell storing logic '0' ($Q = 0\text{ V}$), charge flows from the precharged bitline $BL$ through the access transistor and the driver (pull-down) NMOS to ground, developing a sensing differential $\Delta V_{BL}$. This creates a resistive voltage divider between the access transistor and the driver transistor. To guarantee read stability and avoid destructive read upsets, the voltage bump at node $Q$ must remain strictly below the threshold voltage of the opposing driver NMOS ($V_{th,n}$). This requirement dictates that the driver transistor must be significantly stronger than the access transistor, defined by the Cell Ratio: $CR = \frac{(W/L)_{\text{driver}}}{(W/L)_{\text{access}}} = \frac{W_n / L_n}{W_a / L_a} \geq 1.2$.

3. Write Operation and Pull-up Ratio ($PR$): During a write operation, the bitlines are driven by external write buffers to complementary logic states representing the input data, and $WL$ is pulsed high. To successfully write a logic '0' into a node holding '1', the access transistor must overpower the pull-up PMOS transistor and pull the internal node voltage below the inverter switching threshold, triggering regenerative latch switching. To guarantee writeability, the pull-up PMOS must be weaker than the access NMOS, defined by the Pull-up Ratio: $PR = \frac{(W/L)_{\text{pullup}}}{(W/L)_{\text{access}}} = \frac{W_p / L_p}{W_a / L_a} \leq 0.6$.

4. Data Retention (Hold Mode): In standby mode, the Wordline is held at logic low ($WL = 0\text{ V}$), turning off the access transistors and isolating the storage latch from the bitline capacitances. The positive feedback continuously maintains the latched complementary voltages with only minute static leakage currents.

sections.title: CONCLUSION
text: 1. The 6T SRAM cell was successfully designed and simulated in 180nm CMOS technology, achieving a Cell Ratio ($CR = 12.00$) and Pull-up Ratio ($PR = 0.50$) that satisfy the read-stability and writeability criteria.

2. Transient simulations verified robust functionality across all states: successfully demonstrating Write '1', data retention, Write '0', and non-destructive differential Read '0' without read disturbance.
